items.reason: Whole-set setup prints the set identifier, resolved Runtime path, and routed binding kind before the status table.
Header rendering is unconditional, including runs inside the bound checkout.
The invocation line appears only when directory comparison finds a different location.
Routing propagates BoundDefault into the binding-recorded announcement.
The old conditional bound-checkout message is removed.
Single-task HITL targets return through runTargetedHITLGate before reaching the new current-checkout line.
Successful task execution emits one green done result line.
Commit SHA or verified no-op detail prints immediately beneath the done line.
Whole-set execution no longer calls the old completion renderer; each ending emits one result.
Retry-exhausted task failures retain failed status and emit one red failed line.
Provider-exhausted walks emit one red out-of-agents line and preserve open status.
Quota parking emits a yellow quota-paused line naming the selected preset.
Interrupted execution errors map to the yellow interrupted result line.
Blocked and Deferred remain set-level reports; executed tasks retain their own results.
Attempt narration, timing breakdowns, and exhausted-walk narration remain intact.
The shared output layer preserves complete text and suppresses ANSI for redirected output.
Header styling and result colors use the existing terminal and NO_COLOR handling.
Added rendering writes only to output writers and introduces no journal operations.

scores.rationale: Clear, localized implementation with useful behavioral tests; single-task HITL coverage misses a real omission, and the supplied diff was reviewed statically.

accepted.behaviour: A single-task file run (`<set>/<file>.md`) prints no Drain header and instead prints a line stating it runs in the current checkout, naming that path.
accepted.reason: The spec asks for the current-checkout line on every single-task file run. The Reference skips it for HITL tasks, which return early through runTargetedHITLGate.
